papers.title: Higher rewriting for strong linearly distributive coherence
papers.abstract: Rewriting is a computational method to solve word problems: deciding whether two compound expressions, or words, are equivalent with respect to a set of identities. Higher rewriting generalizes rewriting to higher-dimensional words, or cells, in higher categories. Following Guiraud and Malbos, we use higher rewriting to generalize Mac Lane's coherence theorem. Our result concerns strong linearly distributive categories: categories equipped with two unital tensor products related by invertible distributors. We show that in a strong linearly distributive category every formal diagram commutes.

papers.title: P{\l}onka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
papers.abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{P{\l}onka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for P{\l}onka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.

papers.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
papers.abstract: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.

papers.title: Partial $F$-invariants and cluster categorifications
papers.abstract: The $F$-invariant in cluster algebras is a combinatorial invariant that unifies the $E$-invariant from additive categorification and the $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant from monoidal categorification. In this paper, we study its refinement, the partial $F$-invariant, and establish its mutation formula under changes of the initial seed. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Reading, which asserts that the non-compatible cluster variables can be separated by sign-coherence of $g$-vectors upon varying the initial seed. We further show that, for cluster monomials, the partial $F$-invariants coincide with both the partial $E$-invariants for reachable decorated representations of quivers with potentials and the pole orders of normalized $R$-matrices (or partial $\mathfrak{d}$-invariants) for finite-dimensional reachable simple modules over quantum affine algebras. As consequences, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the pole orders for reachable simple modules in terms of $q$-characters; we verify the conjectural explicit formula for the pole orders between Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules.

papers.title: On the Orthogonal Group of Quadratic Modules
papers.abstract: We classify the conjugacy classes of isometries in the orthogonal group of regular quadratic modules over Artinian local rings with finite residue fields, provided that the characteristic is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry. (More generally, the same classification holds over Henselian local rings with finite residue fields, such as the ring of $p$-adic integers.) The main idea is to lift results over finite fields to local rings by using the Henselian property. By applying these results to the residue class rings $\mathbb{Z}/(p^l)$, we also obtain a classification of the conjugacy classes of isometries of discriminant forms, under the condition that the order of the discriminant form is odd and coprime to the order of the isometry.

papers.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge. Propagating this gap through the PBW filtration of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$, for every nonscalar element, we construct an alternating adjoint operator that lowers its order by exactly one. As applications, we compute the annihilators of all representations with nonzero central character, prove a strengthened form of Etingof's conjecture on nonsplit extensions of $W$-modules, and reduce the classification of prime ideals of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})$ to those of $\mathrm{U}(W)$.

papers.title: The squared antipode of a twisted function algebra is locally unipotent
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a proalgebraic group over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $F:{\rm Rep}(G)\to {\rm Vect}(k)$ be a dimension-preserving tensor functor, possibly nonsymmetric. We prove that a tensor automorphism $T$ of $F$ is locally unipotent if and only if its trace on $F(V)$ equals ${\rm dim} V$ for every $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$. Applied to the Drinfeld element of a dual twisted function algebra $(\mathcal{O}(G)^J)^*$, this proves our conjecture from 2000 that the square of the antipode in $\mathcal{O}(G)^J$ is locally unipotent (arXiv:0002128). Without the trace assumption, we show that for any $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$ the eigenvalues of $T$ on $F(V)$ determine, modulo roots of unity, its eigenvalues on $F(\mathbb{S}^\nu V)$ for every Schur functor $\mathbb{S}^\nu$. The proof combines the Koszul identity, polynomial growth of symmetric powers, Fourier inversion, and congruences for Newton sums.

papers.title: Link invariants from charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators
papers.abstract: Turaev's enhanced Yang--Baxter operators produce invariants of oriented links from solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation. If the enhancing endomorphism is diagonal with generic eigenvalues, Turaev's compatibility condition forces the Yang--Baxter operator $R$ to be charge-conserving, that is, to send each $e_i\otimes e_j$ into the span of $e_i\otimes e_j$ and $e_j\otimes e_i$. Charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators were classified by Martin and Rowell. Building on their classification, we determine all enhancements of charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators with diagonal enhancing endomorphism, and we identify the resulting link invariants. The link invariant associated with such an enhancement is a sum over the colourings of the components of the link by the connected components of $R$, in which each monochromatic sublink contributes a specialization of the HOMFLY--PT polynomial and different colours interact only through linking numbers. Every such state sum arises in this way.

papers.title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally. The proof uses Schremmer's results on affine Bruhat order and Demazure products, together with a theorem that we prove for arbitrary Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Weakly Pointed Fusion $\Pi$-supercategories over fields of characteristic not two
papers.abstract: We study a class of weakly pointed fusion $\Pi$-supercategories over a field $k$ of characteristic not equal to $2$, with unit $\mathbf 1$ satisfying $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf 1) = k$. Assuming the existence of a Brauer--Wall reference category over $k$, we classify these categories up to monoidal equivalence. We show that Brauer--Wall reference categories exist for $k = \mathbb C, \mathbb R$ but not for $k = \mathbb F_5$. For each finite group $G$, we also study a product of these categories equipped with a $G$-grading and define a group $\mathcal T_k(G)$, giving an explicit formula for the multiplication in terms of group cochains for $k = \mathbb C$ and $\mathbb R$.

papers.title: A Syntactic Approach to Ulmer's Bialgebras
papers.abstract: Ulmer proposed to view a bialgebraic structure on an object $x$ as a structure map $f\colon Fx\to Gx$ satisfying an equation $\alpha_{(x,f)} = \beta_{(x,f)}$ of natural transformations. This perspective is powerful enough to account for many algebraic and coalgebraic structures, such as varieties of universal algebra, categories of algebras over a PROP, an operad or a monad. We develop Ulmer's bialgebras within a $2$-categorical setting with PIE limits, where structure maps are abstracted by inserters and their equations by equifiers. A syntax of signatures, theories and models is then used to produce these bialgebraic structures. The syntax of the commutative diagrams defining Hopf algebras can be used, as is, to define the $0$-cell of Hopf algebras within any symmetric pseudomonoid in a $2$-category with PIE limits. In this setting, we show that lax morphisms of models induce morphisms between the objects of algebras, extending the classical result lifting a lax monoidal functor to a functor between the categories of internal monoids. Since the construction of the object of bialgebras is expressed entirely in terms of PIE limits, we show that Kan extensions, accessibility, local presentability, orthogonal factorization systems, regularity, and Barr-exactness lift along the construction under suitable assumptions. A bi-dense class of objects allows us to transfer monadicity and local presentability results to formal settings. Finally, we construct a bi-dense class of $\V$-categories with at most three objects, where $\V$ is any monoidal category with an absorbing initial object.

papers.title: New approaches to finite generation of cohomology rings
papers.abstract: In support variety theory, representations of a finite dimensional (Hopf) algebra $A$ can be studied geometrically by associating any representation of $A$ to an algebraic variety using the cohomology ring of $A$. An essential assumption in this theory is the finite generation condition for the cohomology ring of $A$ and that for the corresponding modules. In this paper, we introduce various approaches to study the finite generation condition. First, for any finite dimensional Hopf algebra $A$, we show that the finite generation condition on $A$-modules can be replaced by a condition on any affine commutative $A$-module algebra $R$ under the assumption that $R$ is integral over its invariant subring $R^A$. Next, we use a spectral sequence argument to show that a finite generation condition holds for certain filtered, smash and crossed product algebras in positive characteristic if the related spectral sequences collapse. Finally, if $A$ is defined over a number field over the rationals, we construct another finite dimensional Hopf algebra $A'$ over a finite field, where $A$ can be viewed as a deformation of $A'$, and prove that if the finite generation condition holds for $A'$, then the same condition holds for $A$.

papers.title: On Frobenius-Schur exponent bounds
papers.abstract: We study bounds on the Frobenius--Schur exponent of spherical fusion categories in terms of their global dimension, generalizing bounds from the representation theory of finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebras. Our main result is that if the Frobenius--Schur exponent of a modular fusion category is a power of a prime $p$, then it is bounded by the norm of its global dimension when $p$ is odd, and by four times the norm of its global dimension when $p=2$; these bounds are optimal. Moreover, it is bounded by a constant multiple of the geometric mean of the Galois conjugates of its global dimension, which is much smaller when the global dimension is irrational, and a bound of this type is proven for each prime power dividing the Frobenius--Schur exponent of an arbitrary modular or spherical fusion category. Under pseudounitarity, we describe all modular and spherical fusion categories whose Frobenius--Schur exponent is a prime power and at least the norm (respectively, the square of the norm) of their global dimension, using a classification of modular fusion categories of Frobenius--Perron dimension $p^n$ for $n\leq5$.

papers.title: Free wreath products by finite group duals
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb G$ be a compact quantum group and let $\Lambda$ be a finite group. We study $\mathbb W(\mathbb G,\Lambda):=\mathbb G\wr_{*,\beta_\Lambda}\widehat{\Lambda}$, a natural family parallel to Bichon's free wreath products $\mathbb G\wr_*S_N^+$. We obtain an explicit formula for the Haar state of $\mathbb W(\mathbb G,\Lambda)$. Under natural Kac-type factoriality assumptions, we also derive central decompositions of the associated von Neumann and reduced C*-algebras, with full ${\rm II}_1$-factor and simple unique-trace summands.

papers.title: Symmetry of some noncommutative sphere algebras
papers.abstract: Two known $q$-deformed (or `quantum') $7$-spheres, both denoted $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ in the literature, may be distinguished by the presence or absence of symmetry under $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$. The quaternionic version of $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ has been shown by Brain and Landi to support such a symmetry. Here we show that this is not the case for the older $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ introduced by Vaksman and Soibelman: and as a consequence, these quantum $7$-spheres are not isomorphic.
